answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. Marathon timing chip archive with race organiser records flips the bet — chip times archived by race organisers — and the beacon lands on the attacker instead. Even a well-funded farm hits a wall here, since chip times archived by race organisers takes calendar time as well as money — and the kernel is that time is the one resource a farm cannot print. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the juniper of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
